active.title: Cycle the County Road Loop, Prince Edward County
active.description: PEC's back roads deliver some of the best cycling in Eastern Ontario — rolling farm country, vineyard-lined lanes, and glimpses of Lake Ontario on both sides. Rent a bike in Picton if you haven't brought one.
active.bonus: Complete a 30+ km loop without stopping to check your phone for directions — plan the route before you roll.

active.title: Walk the Moira River Trail, Belleville
active.description: The trail system along the Moira River winds through Belleville's oldest parks from Proctor Park all the way to the Bay of Quinte waterfront — more serene than it has any right to be for a walk that starts downtown.
active.bonus: Walk the full route from Proctor Park to the waterfront without retracing your steps. Find a way around.

active.title: Paddleboard the Bay of Quinte at Belleville
active.description: The long, sheltered bay between Belleville and Prince Edward County sits flat most mornings — calm enough for a first open-water paddle and big enough that you'll feel the scale of it once you're out there.
active.bonus: Paddle far enough out that you can see both the Belleville waterfront and the PEC shoreline at the same time.

active.title: Mountain Bike Macaulay Mountain Conservation Area, Picton
active.description: The trail network above Picton is Prince Edward County's best-kept outdoor secret — hardpack singletrack through mixed forest with enough elevation change and technical sections to feel like a real ride.
active.bonus: Run the main descent without braking on the straight sections. Full commitment.

social.title: Saturday at Belleville Farmers Market
social.description: One of Eastern Ontario's best year-round markets runs in downtown Belleville with vendors who grow, raise, or make everything they sell — it's the most honest version of the local food scene, and the most affordable.
social.bonus: Buy one thing from a vendor you have to ask about. Cook or eat it the same day.

social.title: Patio Night on Belleville's Front Street
social.description: Belleville's main street comes alive on summer evenings with riverside patios, a walkable stretch of bars and restaurants, and a downtown that's been quietly earning its reputation for years.
social.bonus: End the night somewhere you found by walking, not by searching.

social.title: Wine Tasting at Closson Chase Vineyards
social.description: One of Prince Edward County's most respected wineries sits on a limestone ridge in Hillier with a tasting room that earns every word of its reputation — serious estate wines in an honest building.
social.bonus: Taste every wine in the flight and ask the sommelier which one they'd drink tonight. Order that one.

social.title: Golden Hour at Huff Estates Winery Terrace
social.description: Huff's estate in Bloomfield is the social heart of PEC wine country — the terrace fills at 4pm with cyclists finishing the county loop and regulars who never really left, and the light across the vineyard at golden hour is the reason everyone comes back.
social.bonus: Stay until the terrace empties out and get a quiet pour before closing. It's always the better glass.

chill.title: Sunset at Belleville Waterfront Park
chill.description: The Bay of Quinte at sunset from Belleville's downtown waterfront is a quietly overlooked thing — the water goes flat gold as the sun drops behind Prince Edward County and the marina goes still.
chill.bonus: Put your phone in your bag for the full duration of sunset. Not airplane mode — bag.

chill.title: Afternoon on Sandbanks Dunes Beach, PEC
chill.description: The world's largest freshwater baymouth barrier dunes drop into impossibly shallow, warm lake water — the sand is fine, the colour is Caribbean, and everyone there has agreed to say nothing to ruin it.
chill.bonus: Walk the full dune crest from one end to the other before you get in the water.

chill.title: Lake on the Mountain, Prince Edward County
chill.description: A natural lake sits 60 metres above Lake Ontario with no visible inlet and no scientific consensus on where the water comes from — the overhang view of the lake, the ferry crossing below, and the Loyalist Parkway is something you can't explain until you've seen it.
chill.bonus: Read about the geology before you go. Try to find the evidence yourself when you're standing there.

chill.title: Sunrise at Presqu'ile Provincial Park Beach
chill.description: The beach at Presqu'ile faces east across a marsh-lined bay — fall migration brings thousands of birds through in a single morning, and even off-season the dawn light on the water and the silence earns the drive from Belleville.
chill.bonus: Arrive before the sun clears the horizon. If you miss first light, it doesn't count.

foodie.title: Breakfast at The Acoustic Grill, Picton
foodie.description: Picton's most honest breakfast spot serves the county from first light — local ingredients, no affectation, and a room that fills with cyclists, cottagers, and year-round island residents who all have a usual order.
foodie.bonus: Order something you haven't had for breakfast before. No eggs and toast if that's your default.

foodie.title: Lunch on the Terrace at Drake Devonshire, Wellington
foodie.description: Drake's lakefront property in Wellington serves one of the best casual farm-to-table lunches in Ontario on a terrace that looks across Prince Edward Bay — come post-ride and stay for longer than you planned.
foodie.bonus: Order something sourced from PEC and ask your server exactly where it came from.

foodie.title: Craft Beer and Kitchen at Parsons Brewing, Picton
foodie.description: PEC's most serious craft brewery runs a kitchen that matches the beer program — a local ingredients menu that would surprise anyone who assumed this was just a tasting room.
foodie.bonus: Order their most unusual seasonal beer without reading the description first. Just say yes when they describe it.

foodie.title: Wood-Fired Pizza and Pinot at Norman Hardie Winery
foodie.description: The most celebrated natural wine producer in Ontario serves wood-fired Neapolitan pizza in a simple farm building surrounded by pinot noir vines — it's genuinely among the best lunches you can eat anywhere in Canada.
foodie.bonus: Bring someone who knows nothing about natural wine and explain one thing about it to them before the first glass arrives.

adventure.title: Canoe the Moira River to the Bay of Quinte
adventure.description: The Moira River winds through Belleville's eastern edge before emptying into the Bay of Quinte — a flatwater paddle that feels genuinely wild for a river you can drive across in the middle of the city.
adventure.bonus: Take the river all the way to the bay and cross to the Prince Edward County shore before turning back.

adventure.title: Paddle the First Lock: Trent-Severn from Trenton
adventure.description: The mouth of the Trent River in Trenton is the start of a 386-km inland waterway that runs all the way to Georgian Bay — paddle upstream through Lock 1 and into the river proper for a feel of what it means to go the long way.
adventure.bonus: Pass through a lock under human power. Stay in the chamber and feel the water rise before you exit.

adventure.title: Ice Skating on the Bay of Quinte
adventure.description: In a real winter the inner Bay of Quinte freezes flat enough that locals drive out, clear a rink, and skate a surface sometimes hundreds of metres wide — it's the most distinctly Canadian thing you can do in the region.
adventure.bonus: Skate far enough from shore that you can't see your car. Then skate back.

adventure.title: Sunset Sea Kayak from Picton Harbour
adventure.description: Paddle out of Picton's sheltered harbour into the open bay at golden hour with the county's limestone bluffs on one side and the mainland hills across the water — the light at dusk here is something you don't find inland.
adventure.bonus: Stay on the water until dark and navigate back by the harbour lights alone.
